title: Audit logs & admin activity review - Apex Payments
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Apex Payments through what audit logs capture (admin actions, API calls, token usage), export and retention options, KMS/encryption details, and SSO/RBAC integration. Customer asked about long-term retention, export to SIEM, and residency; Redwood proposed retention tiers, S3-compatible export, and a pilot to validate format and event fidelity.

header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO - Apex), Priya Nair (Security Engineer - Apex), Diane Holt (Compliance Manager - Apex)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Marcus: Marcus here.
[00:09] Priya: Priya on the line.
[00:11] Diane: Diane joining.
[00:14] Elena (Redwood SE): Elena here from Redwood, excited to dig into the audit logs and admin activity.
[00:18] Samir: Goal today is to cover what we capture, export options, retention, and KMS/encryption questions you raised. We'll leave time for compliance specifics.
[00:27] Marcus: Sounds good. High level, we need to understand what events we get and how long they live, and how we can ship them to our SIEM.
[00:34] Priya: Also need clarity on admin activity, role changes, API key creation, deletion, and any access to customer data.
[00:41] Elena: Absolutely. On the audit logs side we capture admin-level events (user and role creation/deletion/role assignment), API token lifecycle (create/rotate/revoke), admin console logins, SSO auth attempts (success/fail), model deployment and rollback events, configuration changes to dedicated/private deployments, and data export actions.
[01:05] Priya: When you say "data export actions" do you mean admin-triggered exports of logs or customer data?
[01:11] Elena: Primarily export of logs and configuration. For content-level exports we log the action and the initiating principal but we don't store content in logs. There is a reference to the object ID and a job ID so you can correlate.
[01:22] Diane: Good. We need to show auditors that admin actions are immutable and show who did what and when. How immutable are the logs? Can they be altered?
[01:30] Elena: Logs are write-once within the system and maintain append-only storage. For hosted customers, we provide export hooks to push to your S3 or to a syslog/Splunk endpoint for long-term retention under your control. If you pull logs to your S3 bucket and apply your retention/immutability policies (like object lock), that satisfies auditors.
[01:47] Marcus: Ok, export options — what formats and delivery mechanisms do you support?
[01:51] Elena: We export in newline-delimited JSON by default, optional CSV for some tables. Delivery options: push to S3 (customer bucket via cross-account role), send to syslog/UDP/TCP endpoint, or forward to common SIEMs (Splunk HTTP event collector, QRadar). We also have an API to page logs for short-term querying.
[02:10] Priya: Is there a streaming option so we can have near-real time ingestion into Splunk?
[02:14] Elena: Yes. We support near-real-time streaming via a Kafka-compatible endpoint or via streaming to your SIEM's HTTP endpoint. There may be throttles based on plan, but for dedicated/private deployments we can do high-throughput streams.
[02:27] Marcus: Retention — what's default and can we set per-event retention?
[02:31] Samir: Default retention in hosted is 90 days for audit logs, 365 days for admin console events on enterprise plans; Dedicated and Private let you configure retention. We typically provide tiered retention options: 90, 365, and custom multi-year retention — especially for finance/regulatory customers.
[02:50] Diane: We need six years for some records per our regulator — can you support multi-year?
[02:55] Elena: For sure — if you export to your S3 with lifecycle/GLACIER archival that meets multi-year retention. For hosted-only retention we can configure longer retention but for the strongest guarantees we recommend export to your own storage.
[03:06] Priya: How do you handle PII/PII masking in logs? We can't have raw customer PII in logs.
[03:11] Elena: We avoid logging sensitive content; the logs capture metadata: user IDs (internal), asset IDs, job IDs, and hashes. We do not capture prompt or content payloads in audit logs. There are separate request logs for debugging that can be configured with content redaction; we recommend those be used carefully and only exported to customer-controlled storage if needed.
[03:30] Marcus: KMS/encryption — who holds the keys?
[03:33] Samir: By default, logs at rest are encrypted with Redwood-managed keys (KMS). For enterprise customers we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in your cloud account for Dedicated and Private, and we can integrate with your KMS/HSM. For hosted we also offer BYOK where you provide a key we can wrap.
[03:51] Priya: If we bring our own key, can we revoke and make logs unreadable from your side? That's part of our policy.
[03:58] Elena: If you use your own KMS key for the export bucket, you control access. For server-side Redwood-managed storage, revocation of a key is destructive; we can discuss key rotation policies. For Dedicated/Private the CMK is in your account so you control revocation.
[04:13] Diane: Audit trail for SSO/RBAC — do you log SAML assertions and attributes or only success/failure events?
[04:19] Elena: We log SSO events including timestamp, principal identifier (nameID), assertion ID reference, success/failure, and some attributes like issuer. We do not persist full assertion payloads by default. For deeper forensic needs we can capture assertion dumps into customer-controlled storage under explicit agreement.
[04:36] Priya: Can we map those entries to our identity provider logs for correlation?
[04:40] Elena: Yes — every SSO event includes correlation IDs and timestamps to join with IdP logs. We also can include raw assertion IDs to match in Okta/Azure logs.
[04:49] Marcus: For admin activity, do you include IP addresses and geo?
[04:53] Elena: We capture source IP, region, user agent, and whether the request came from the control plane or API. For private deployments that may be internal IPs depending on network mode.
[05:03] Priya: Regarding evidence for auditors, do you provide signed logs or a chain-of-custody?
[05:08] Samir: We can provide log export with checksums and timestamped manifests. For higher assurance we can deliver signed manifests and work with you to include storage-level immutability (S3 Object Lock) for chain-of-custody.
[05:21] Diane: Nice. On the SIEM mapping, we need field mappings for Splunk and QRadar — can you share that?
[05:27] Elena: Yes, we'll share a mapping. We'll also include example queries and a sample workbook.
[05:33] Marcus: Any limitations we should know about for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[05:36] Elena: Hosted: default retention and streaming available but subject to plan throttles. Dedicated: you get dedicated compute and higher throughput for streaming exports, plus cross-account S3 export and CMK support. Private/on-prem: you own storage and keying entirely and there's no cross-account concern.
[05:53] Priya: For the pilot, we want to validate event fidelity and timing to our SIEM — what's a realistic sampling window?
[05:59] Samir: A week of live streaming at production-ish volume is typical to validate volume and schema. We can also do a shortproof two-day run with representative traffic.
[06:09] Diane: On regulatory paperwork, can you share your SOC 2 and ISO artifacts?
[06:12] Samir: Yes, we'll send SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 summary pack, plus the audit-log schema and export samples.
[06:20] Marcus: A couple of detailed questions — will logs show who rolled back a model or who started a batch job that accessed sensitive connectors?
[06:28] Elena: Yes, model deployment/rollback events include actor, timestamp, model version, and job ID. Connector access events log the initiating identity and connector ID; we do not log connector data but we log the operation.
[06:39] Priya: How about retention for API key rotation history — do you keep old key identifiers so we can prove rotation?
[06:46] Elena: We keep key lifecycle events including key ID create/rotate/revoke and the actor. We do not store key material.
[06:54] Marcus: Any known gaps that would block us from using hosted?
[06:58] Diane: For example, if auditors insist logs must be kept on customer-owned HSM encrypted storage only.
[07:04] Samir: That would push towards Dedicated or Private. Hosted has options but the strongest guarantees (customer CMKs and customer-owned bucket with object lock) are available with Dedicated/private patterns and cross-account S3 export.
[07:18] Priya: About format — can we get searchable fields for user, action, target_resource, ip, timestamp, request_id?
[07:24] Elena: Yes, that's the default schema. We'll include the schema doc in the package.
[07:29] Marcus: OK. One more: retention auditing — can Redwood show us retention enforcement logs?
[07:35] Elena: We record retention policy changes as config events. When exports run we also log the export job status. For data lifecycle enforcement (S3 deletion or GLACIER transition) you'll have the storage provider's audit trail; we log the action that triggered it.
[07:51] Diane: That should be fine.
[07:54] Samir: Next steps recap: we'll send SOC artifacts, the audit log schema, a sample export, SIEM mapping, and propose a pilot window. Priya, Diane, Marcus you'll confirm retention and SIEM endpoints.
[08:08] Priya: We'll get that by the 19th.
[08:11] Marcus: Thanks all.
[08:13] Elena: Thanks, will follow up with links.
[08:16] Samir: Meeting adjourned.
[08:18] (end)
